Used as a shared read primitive across deserialization, file enumeration, scene parsing, mesh loading and file-write paths.

operations.description: Acquire the stream lock with StreamBufferLockViaCriticalSection(a4) using argument 4 as the stream handle.
Perform the actual read: v4 = sub_58806E(a1, a2, a3, a4), forwarding all four arguments unchanged.
Release the lock with AddressRangeCriticalSectionLeave(a4) before returning.
Return the inner read result v4 from sub_58806E unchanged.

Used as a shared synchronous read primitive by deserialization, file enumeration, scene parsing, mesh loading and file-write paths, e.g. BinaryDataDeserialization (0x004054E0), MemoryAllocationWithBufferRead (0x004080F0), FileEnumerationByExtension (0x00421B10), BufferedFileReader (0x00534F90), MeshVertexIndexBufferLoader (0x00550AD0), SceneFileTopLevelParser (0x0055B200) and FileWriteWithBackendDispatch (0x00566C00).

unresolved: The lock/unlock pair is separated by the inner call rather than a symmetric enter/leave helper, and the two lock primitives live at different addresses (0x0058C1B1 vs 0x0058C203); whether they guard the same underlying critical section is inferred from naming, not proven here.
sub_58806E is the actual read implementation but its body is not in this packet; the exact read semantics of a1/a2/a3 are not established.

functions.name: QuicksortByteBuffer
functions.summary: Iterative quicksort over an array of a2 elements, each a3 bytes, at base address a1, ordered by the caller-supplied comparator a4 (a4 returns <= 0 or >= 0 relative to the pivot). Small subarrays (8 or fewer elements) are handed to sub_5891FE. Partitioning: the middle element is swapped to the front with ByteBufferSwap as the pivot, a Hoare-style scan advances from both ends (left while a4 <= 0, right while a4 >= 0) swapping crossing pairs, and the pivot is placed at the meeting point. Subarray bounds are kept on an explicit stack over the local buffers v14/v15 with depth counter v17; the larger partition is processed in place while the smaller is pushed, bounding stack depth.

operations.description: If the element count a2 is less than 2 or the element size a3 is zero, return immediately (nothing sortable).
Initialize the sort: v5 = a1 + a3 * (a2 - 1) (address of the last element); set up the explicit subarray-bound stacks v19/v18 over the local buffers v14/v15 and the depth counter v17.
Compute the current subarray's element count v6 = (v5 - a1) / a3 + 1.
If v6 <= 8, hand the small range to sub_5891FE(a1, v5, a3, a4) and continue with the next subarray taken from the stack.
Swap the middle element (a1 + a3 * (v6 >> 1)) to the front with ByteBufferSwap, making it the pivot.

Hoare partition: advance v16 from the left while a4(element) <= 0, advance i from the right while a4(element) >= 0, and swap each crossing pair with ByteBufferSwap(v16, i, a3), repeating until the scans meet.
Swap the pivot back into its final position with ByteBufferSwap(a1, i, a3) at the scan meeting point.
Record v9 = v16 (start of the right partition) and compare the partition sizes (int)(i - a1 - 1) and (int)(v5 - v16) to choose which side is processed next and which is pushed.

Push the deferred subarray bounds onto the explicit stack (v19/v18 with depth counter v17) and select the next subarray to process: the left partition ending at i - a3 or the right partition starting at v9.
Pop a subarray from the stack; when the depth counter v17 goes below zero the stack is empty and the function returns.

unresolved: sub_5891FE (the small-range handler) is assumed to be the terminal insertion-style sorter, but its body is outside this function.
The comparator convention (a4's sign relative to the pivot on both scan sides) is inferred from the conditions a4(v8) <= 0 and a4(i) >= 0; the caller contract is unverified.
The explicit-stack local buffers v14/v15 have no evident size in this decompilation.

functions.name: GetPerThreadDataWithInit
functions.summary: CRT-style per-thread data retrieval. Saves the current GetLastError value, reads the per-thread data block pointer via TlsGetValue(dwTlsIndex). On first access for a thread (null pointer), lazily allocates a 116-byte block with sub_58AB58(1, 116), registers it with TlsSetValue(dwTlsIndex, block), initializes it via TwoFieldInitializer_e0b4 and stamps it with the current thread id and a -1 sentinel; on allocation/registration failure it terminates with CRTAmsgExit(0x10). Finally restores the saved LastError value and returns the per-thread data pointer.

operations.description: Capture GetLastError() into LastError so the TLS setup path can restore it afterward.
Retrieve the per-thread data block via TlsGetValue(dwTlsIndex).
Branch on the TlsGetValue result: a null value means the per-thread block has not been allocated yet on this thread.
Allocate a new per-thread data block with sub_58AB58(1, 116) (116-byte block).
Register the newly allocated block with TlsSetValue(dwTlsIndex, block); if the allocation or registration fails, terminate with CRTAmsgExit(0x10).
Initialize fields of the new block via TwoFieldInitializer_e0b4.
Capture GetCurrentThreadId() to stamp the block with the owning thread id.
Stamp the block: Value[1] = -1 and Value[0] = current thread id.
Restore the saved LastError value via SetLastError so the TLS machinery does not disturb the caller's error state.
Return the per-thread data pointer (newly created on first access, previously stored otherwise).

unresolved: The per-thread block layout (beyond Value[0] thread id and Value[1] = -1 sentinel) is unknown; the fields initialized by TwoFieldInitializer_e0b4 are not enumerated here.
The identity of the per-thread structure's owner is unknown; treated as an unverified CRT-owned block.
The allocation size semantics of sub_58AB58(1, 116) (element count / element size vs byte count) are unverified.
